Sports.title: World Cup final descends into violence at full-time whistle as Spain and Argentina players clash in ugly scenes
Sports.content:
The World Cup final descended into outrageous scenes as fights broke out among the two sets of players.

Some of Argentina's players lost their heads as Spain's substitutes and staff ran on to the pitch to celebrate their 1-0 win against the South Americans.

Ferran Torres scored a 106th-minute winner after Enzo Fernandez had been sent off in the 93rd minute for a desperately poor Argentina side.

After the whistle, Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes was sent off for putting his hand on Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground. Argentina's Thiago Almada was also involved.

Micah Richards said of their behaviour on the BBC: 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time.

'Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest. Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Argentina's Leandro Paredes was sent off after the whistle for getting violent with Spain

Several stars clashed after Spain's 1-0 win as Argentina - but the South Americans started it

Joe Hart added: 'Disgusting behaviour. There was one man on that pitch with class and that was Lionel Messi.'

Wayne Rooney said: 'Rooney: 'It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this from Argentina before. It's just sad, very poor from them.

'If you lose a game of football, be graceful. It's a reaction to them being outplayed. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves it's well.'

Argentina were thuggish throughout the World Cup final, as they had been against England in the semis.

Fernandez complained against his dimissal for a second yellow but his late foul on Pau Cubarsi, which sent the defender flying, was atrocious.

Paredes was also fortunate to not be sent off in regular time for a foul on the edge of the box which presented Lamine Yamal with a last-breath free-kick before extra-time.

More to follow.

Sports.title: Spain 1 Argentina 0 PLAYER RATINGS: Which two stars received 3/10 after dreadful displays? Who was 'imperious' but faded? And which Premier League stalwart delivered a 'shocking' first-half?
Sports.content:
Ferran Torres wrote his name into Spanish football history after scoring in the 106th minute of the World Cup final to break the hearts of Argentina and Lionel Messi.

The substitute, who smashed his finish into the roof of the net, reclaimed deserved glory for La Roja for the first time since 2010 after their opponents managed just two shots across the entirety of the match.

Spain's elegance and discipline was contrasted with the brutish skulduggery of Argentina, who saw Enzo Fernandez sent off in the 93rd minute. His midfield counterpart, Leandro Paredes, was also shown his marching orders after a violent clash at full-time.

Daily Mail Sport's CRAIG HOPE was at the MetLife Stadium to bring you our player ratings.

Spain (4-2-3-1)

Unai Simon - 6

Twice off his line in a flash to clear after balls were dropped in behind for Messi and Alvarez to chase. But there was not a save to make.

Pedro Porro - 6

Hardly troubled in defence so took that opportunity to join attack, as he likes to. Heavily involved, - more than 120 touches - but crosses rarely found intended target.

Pau Cubarsi - 8

Tried to get his team going with forward passes from deep, including one to get Yamal away. Was super cool in defence, too. He’s a star.

Aymeric Laporte - 7

Rarely flustered at the back so subdued was Messi and thought he’d won it with late header plucked on goal-line by Martinez.

Marc Cucurella - 7

Typically snappy in his challenges and, like Porro, poured forward when realising how passive Argentina were. Nearly scored opener with low drill wide.

Rodri - 7

Imperious early on and everything went through him. He looked like the grown-up in midfield battle. That influence faded and he could not find the pass to break stubborn Argentina.

Rodri dictated the game for Spain in midfield

Fabian Ruiz - 6

A threat amid otherwise mundane first half, but way below best. Came into it more after break and dribble led to good chance for Torres. Much like whole tournament, not the final we’d hoped for from him.

Lamine Yamal - 7

A threat amid otherwise mundane first half, but still below best. Came into it more after break and dribble led to good chance for Torres. Much like whole tournament, not really the final we’d hoped for from him, but played his part.

Dani Olmo - 6

Like many of Spain’s other attacking starters he just could not produce that moment of inspiration. Not as peripheral as the others, but no real impact.

Alex Baena - 4

No end product from left wing and was a surprise he stayed on until 75th minute. A big chance to impress but Atletico Madrid man did not take it.

Mikel Oyarzabal - 5

A star of the tournament but this was a game to forget on the biggest occasion. One shot on target and one touch in area before making way just after hour.

Substitutes

Ferran Torres (on for Oyarzabal 62) - 8

Pedri (on for Fabian Ruiz 62) - 7

Mikel Merino (on for Olmo 75) - 6

Nico Williams (on for Baena 75) - 9

Martin Zubimendi (on for Rodri 99) - 6

Eric Garcia (on for Laporte 99) - 6

Manager: Luis de la Fuente - 8

Has now delivered the World Cup and European Championship. They made hard work of this and should have been good enough to win in normal time, but introduction of Williams and Torres was the inspiration Spain needed.

Ferran Torres came off the bench to score Spain's winner

Argentina (4-4-2)

Emiliano Martinez - 8

Improvised early on to deny Yamal and that was the first of 11 saves. Kept his team in the game and had no chance with winner. Easily Argentina’s best.

Gonzalo Montiel - 6

Saved likely goal when stealing from toe of Cucurella in penalty area after half-time, but that was his last involvement. Had been solid before that.

Cristian Romero - 6

Never far from the action, as is his way, and got the better of Oyarzabal in duel with Spain’s five-goal striker. Seemed to tire after exertions of semi versus England.

Lisandro Martinez - 5

Injury nightmare just before half-time when hurting his thigh as he brought down Rodri. Long balls had been wasteful to that point.

Enzo Fernandez became the sixth player to be sent off during a World Cup final

Nicolas Tagliafico - 7

Tasked with keeping Yamal quiet and, one or two flashes from the Spain winger apart, it was a job he did well. Emerges with credit.

Rodrigo De Paul - 5

His loose pass caused team-mate Lisandro to foul Rodri at expense of booking and injury. Was diligent in defensive work but not good enough on the ball.

Alexis Mac Allister - 4

Shocking first half. Repeatedly found red with stray passes and was lucky to escape yellow for lunge on Olmo. Recovered to put in decent shift but quality still lacking.

Enzo Fernandez - 3

Red card shame on back of untidy display. He set the tone against England but was too passive here, except when committing the two second-half fouls that brought deserved yellows.

Nico Gonzalez - 3

Anonymous and invariably lost the ball when he did get it. Was no surprise to see him hooked at the break after completing only five passes.

Lionel Messi endured a quiet game, touching the ball just once in the first 15 minutes

Lionel Messi - 5

One touch first 15 minutes and that was from kick off. Also pulled out of 50-50 with Simon. Justin Bieber got closer to the penalty area in normal time. Belatedly came to life in final moments and was dangerous. All too late, though.

Julian Alvarez - 4

Tried to do the running while Messi walked but had no service and left the field after 102 minutes without a shot. You could sense his frustration.

Substitutes

Nicolas Otamendi (on for L Martinez 45) 6

Leandro Paredes (on for Gonzalez 46) 4

Nahuel Molina (on for Montiel 58) 5

Giuliano Simeone (on for De Paul 70) 5

Facundo Medina (on for Romero 70) 5

Marcos Senesi (on for Alvarez 102) 5

Manager: Lionel Scaloni - 4

Didn't send out his team with same snarliness as against England and, come the end, they had not even found the target over 120 minutes. A weak defence of their title.

Referee: Slavko Vincic - 5

Sports.title: Spain 1-0 Argentina: Ferran Torres' extra time winner secures World Cup trophy for Luis de la Fuente's side - as Lionel Messi suffers tournament heartbreak
Sports.content:
The voice of Frank Sinatra rang around the MetLife Stadium before the World Cup final. As he sang about facing the ‘final curtain’, the big screen showed footage of Lionel Messi holding aloft the World Cup in Qatar four years ago and being borne shoulder-high by his teammates in triumph. ‘I did it my way,’ Sinatra sang, as the Manhattan skyscrapers shimmered in the distance.

In times when football has lost itself, when it has moved away from those who love it, when it has become enslaved to money and ruled by high ticket prices, when it is led by sycophants and grifters, when it has been assailed by doubts about its integrity and its direction, Messi has always been there to redeem it, doing it his way. This time, in the midst of this drab, angry, bitter, attritional final, doing it his way was not enough.

At a World Cup afflicted by a myriad of controversies, a World Cup with a final saddled with a dirge of a half-time show and hydration breaks that are advertising breaks and President Trump calling Gianni Infantino to lobby, successfully, for Folarin Balogun’s suspension to be lifted, and $1m pitchside seats, seeing Messi play was always enough to make the heart sing.

Even at 39, the greatest player the world has ever seen, has still been the sport’s human shield. Even as Trump and Infantino have danced around the tournament like puppeteers, Messi has worked his magic, scored more goals than anyone apart from Kylian Mbappe and floated above the storms.

Messi has graced his sport for more than 20 years and Argentina’s obstinate, defiant, sometimes desperate run to this World Cup final against Spain was predicated around this being ‘Leo’s last one’. They wanted to do it for him. They wanted to give him the send-off he deserved before he retreated to what remains of his club career with Inter Miami in Major League Soccer.

And so Messi went to the well one last time in the blazing sunshine in New Jersey. Fifteen of his 21 tournament goals have come since his 35th birthday and even though Mbappe had moved ahead of him in the race for the Golden Boot on Saturday evening and ahead of him in the all-time World Cup list, many hoped Messi would put that right on Sunday, too.

Spain have won the World Cup after Ferran Torres' extra time winner against Argentina

Torres smashed in the winner with his left foot after Nico Williams headed the ball back across goal

It was elation for the Spanish players as they celebrated wildly in the corner of the stadium

But it was devastation for Argentina's crestfallen stars, who had fought for their lives

The truth is that when Messi went to the well this time, the well was empty. This was a game too far, even for him. Tom Cruise had given a speech on the pitch before kick-off and this match turned into Messi’s mission impossible.

He was swallowed up in the mediocrity of a final that was at odds with so much of the drama that this World Cup has provided. It was dull and attritional. It was dominated by Spain, who finally turned their advantage into a winning goal in the second period of extra time.

And if many wanted Messi to win, by then not many wanted Argentina to win. They played with a mixture of unabashed thuggery and a desperate lack of ambition. They did not have a single shot, let alone a shot on target. If there was a shred of satisfaction about their defrocking, it was that it came with an overdue red card for Enzo Fernandez, their self-styled enforcer.

So Messi’s final fling fell flat. He did not end the competition with the Golden Boot, he did not win the second World Cup he craved, and he left the international stage after being able to exert precious little influence on his final match. Sport is no respecter of reputation.

Much of the talk before the game had been about a passing of the torch from Messi to Spain’s superstar teenager Lamine Yamal but even if Yamal had more influence than Messi, he has been struggling with the after-effects of a hamstring injury and could not stamp his brilliance on the game.

It was Ferran Torres who made the difference when he came on, Ferran Torres who scored the winner and Ferran Torres who thought he had scored a second before it was ruled out for offside. This was Spain’s second World Cup triumph after 2010. They only conceded one goal in the entire competition. They were the better team by a large margin here.

Torres' goal sparked jubilation for the thousands of Spanish fans inside the stadium

Argentina keeper Emiliano Martinez had been in inspired form before that to keep Spain at bay

There was no fairytale World Cup ending for Lionel Messi who struggled to assert his authority

Enzo Fernandez was sent off at the end of normal time for a reckless second bookable offence

A melee ensued and Messi tried to get Marc Cucurella sent off for covering his mouth

Yamal had the first chance of the game within the opening five minutes. A neat touch from Dani Olmo played Yamal in behind the Argentina defence but he did not hit his shot with enough power or accuracy to beat Emiliano Martinez.

Argentina had not started the game with the same furious intent they showed against England in the semi-final. Not driven by the same visceral resentment, they showed Spain far more respect and allowed them to dictate the tempo of the game.

Spain had only conceded one goal in the tournament before this game but they had a scare early on when Messi raced on to a through ball. He was clean through but Unai Simon sprinted 35 yards out of his goal to clear it and got there just ahead of Argentina’s skipper. Some felt Messi had missed an opportunity. ‘He had to put his body in and he didn't,' Wayne Rooney said.

Alexis Mac Allister scythed down Olmo after 15 minutes but, inexplicably, referee Slavko Vincic, chose not to show him even a yellow card. The Spain fans were infuriated. They are keenly aware of the lenient treatment Argentina have benefited from in this World Cup. ‘Infantino, Infantino,’ they jeered.

The game settled into a kind of stalemate, the antithesis of the Soccer Aid vibe that permeated England’s 3rd place play-off game with France the previous day. There was, at least, a ripple of surprise when the referee booked Lisandro Martinez. It was just about the only decision that had gone Spain’s way all afternoon.

The half-time show came and went in a splurge of underwhelming banality. It was much like the opening 45 minutes, in which Argentina had not managed a single shot on target. Leandro Paredes came on at the interval and was booked within a few minutes for a shove in the back of Max Baena.

Argentina did their best to rile up Spain and there were several flashpoints between the players

Things escalated at full-time when Leandro Paredes clashed with several Spain players

The stands were filled with celebrities, including David Beckham and Tom Cruise (centre)

President Donald Trump also watched on alongside FIFA President Gianni Infantino

Justin Bieber headlined the strange half-time show, which lasted for almost half an hour

Yamal made one burst to the byline midway through the second half and cut the ball back for substitute Ferran Torres. Torres leapt well on the edge of the six-yard box but could only direct his header straight at a grateful Emiliano Martinez.

As the game approached extra time, Argentina imploded. More particularly, Enzo Fernandez imploded. Already on a yellow card, he launched himself into a tackle on Pau Cubarsi and caught the defender’s trailing foot. Cubarsi cart-wheeled into the air and Fernandez was shown a second yellow. It felt like a little karma for the rough-house tactics he had inflicted on England in Atlanta and for which he had escaped without punishment.

Increasingly, only Emiliano Martinez kept Argentina in the game. He saved well from a Yamal free kick and then, early in extra time, from a glancing header by Nico Williams. Spain thought they had scored when Martinez spilled the ball under a challenge but VAR ruled that he had been fouled. It felt like another generous decision towards Argentina.

Spain missed the best chance of the match when Arsenal’s Mikel Merino glanced a header wide from close range near the end of the first half of extra time but they finally broke the deadlock after 106 minutes when Williams nodded the ball back to Torres and Torres smashed the ball past Emiliano Martinez.

Their victory was to be celebrated. Messi’s retreat into the twilight was much to be mourned.

Sports.title: Argentina set unwanted - and barely believable - record after underwhelming World Cup final defeat
Sports.content:
Argentina suffered a historic embarrassment on football’s biggest stage as they turned in a shockingly toothless display in the World Cup final against Spain.

Expectations were sky-high before kick-off at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, with fans anticipating an explosive performance from the reigning champions.

However, instead, the crowd in East Rutherford was subjected to a staggering lack of attacking ambition from Lionel Scaloni's side, as they fell to a 1-0 defeat on the day.

The underwhelming display saw the holders write their names into the history books for all the wrong reasons by setting an unwanted all-time tournament record.

The defending champions became the first team in history to fail to record a single shot of any kind during the initial 90 minutes of a World Cup final.

Lionel Messi and Julian Alvarez were left utterly isolated upfront, starved of service as the midfield struggled to string passes together or breach the Spanish press.

Argentina failed to record a single shot in 90 minutes during Sunday's World Cup final

Lionel Messi and Co. were defeated 1-0 by Spain after an underwhelming clash in New Jersey

The incredible statistic painted a clear picture of Spain's tactical superiority, with the European champions dominating proceedings at a sunny MetLife Stadium.

They did eventually end their attacking struggles during extra time when Messi powered an effort at goal, only to see it blocked by Spain star Mikel Merino.

Argentina eventually ended the game with two total shots, while Spain had 20.

More to follow...

Sports.title: World Cup fans brand FIFA's first-ever halftime show a 'disaster' as Madonna and Bieber's bizarre spectacle divides billions
Sports.content:

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

World Cup fans branded FIFA's controversial first-ever World Cup halftime show starring Madonna and Justin Bieber a 'disaster' on Sunday - as the spectacle divided viewers around the world.

Argentina and Spain superstars Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal were forced to share the stage on Sunday at MetLife Stadium as the high-octane, Super Bowl inspired- performance got underway - which left fans both furious and enthralled in equal measure.

The futuristic segment began with Madonna, 67, singing her 2000 hit Music, accompanied by giddy Brazilian World Cup legends Ronaldo Nazario and Ronaldinho.

The toned music legend was dressed head-to-toe in Saint Laurent, wowing in a pink satin teddy jacket and corset, mini shorts and lace-up boots, paired with stockings as she embraced the soccer icons, before they drove her out into the stadium.

The unlikely trio then posed up on the grass and smiled at the crowds.

Bieber, 32, made a starkly different impact on the crowd as he stepped out with nothing but a guitar to sing a World Cup themed version of his song, Everything Hallelujah.

The singer was bizarrely subbed onto the pitch by Jason Sudeikis, playing his manager alter-ego Ted Lasso.

Madonna and Justin Bieber's performances during the controversial first-ever FIFA World Cup halftime show divided fans on Sunday

Justin Bieber made a starkly different impact on the crowd as he stepped out with nothing but a guitar to sing a World Cup themed version of his song Everything Hallelujah - leaving fans baffled by his song choice

Shakira showed off her toned frame as she performed Dai Dai with Burna Boy

The star looked relaxed as he casually walked onto the pitch before belting out his hit track, adding the final line, 'it's the World Cup, Hallelujah' - with fans left baffled by his song choice.

One fan gave the damning verdict, 'What a disaster this halftime show was. Pre-recorded stuff, no collaborations or surprising moments. Where was Madonna at the end? She could have sung a few lines with Shakira... everything was so weird. So much hype for nothing.'

Yet making clear the division, a second viewer wrote, 'I dislike a lot of things that FIFA does... but THAT halftime show was pretty spectacular.'

Another wrote, 'Who was behind the concept for that haltfime show? Chat GPT?'

Other fans wrote, 'Madonna’s performance was the strangest thing ever, especially followed by the Muppets. The rest of the show was decent. I thought JB’s performance was the best of them all.'

'Light, bright, positive energy. We needed that. Really tired of dark and angry performances.

'It seemed like bieber was off the flow but when Shakira came up after - it all made sense!!!'

'It was great! International and diverse, a positive message, family friendly, and soccer legends hanging with Madonna! Ronaldinho and Ronaldo probably couldn't believe it!'

Bieber's downbeat song choice was undoubtedly one of the major talking points of the performance, with one fan writing, 'Justin Bieber was unfortunately the worst part of the World Cup halftime show.'

Another penned, 'Justin Bieber Hallelujah but this was not the right song choice for the half time show.'

A third typed, 'Buzz killer. Totally sucked . Why choose that song that nobody knows . Beyond me ….' while another wrote, 'terrible song choice.'

Others praised Bieber's performance, writing, 'Justin Bieber looked and sounded great at the World Cup halftime show today!

'Glad he's cleaned up his act!

'Best performance. He knows how to switch people’s moods in a second. That’s extremely difficult to do, most performers couldn’t.'

Shakira returned to the World Cup stage as she flaunted her toned abs in a pink and yellow sequined bodysuit to perform her hit Dai Dai, with Burna Boy, while K-pop sensations BTS regaled the crowd with Dynamite.

Others praised Bieber's performance as 'so good' and worthy of the Super Bowl

K-pop sensations BTS regaled the crowd with Dynamite

BTS captivated the crowds as they continued their return to the stage after mandatory military training

The show delivered a spectacular mix of music, nostalgia and global star power, including a cameo from The Muppets

[IMG 320818273 noborder /] Fans had wildly differing opinions on the spectacular

Former England star Wayne Rooney savaged the controversial World Cup final halftime show, quipping the best part of it was 'when it finished'

Liam Gallagher savaged 'This is like a bad trip', before adding: 'It's a good job I've got my spiritual socks on or that halftime entertainment could have tipped me over the edge'

The show was also blasted by former World Cup England star Wayne Rooney, 41, who joked his favorite part of the show was 'when it finished'.

'To be honest mine was when it finished I like a lot of those artists but to be honest I thought it was c***', he fumed.

'I did honestly. It just didn't get me going, I wanted the football to be back on. It was a bit flat. I like Burna Boy I like Shakira I like Bieber but that was too flat.'

Fans were left in hysterics by Rooney's comment, with one user on X laughing: 'Wayne Rooney on the halftime show actually made me LOL and then 'I like a lot of the artists, but I thought it was c***'.

While Liam Gallagher savaged 'This is like a bad trip', before adding: 'It's a good job I've got my spiritual socks on or that halftime entertainment could have tipped me over the edge'.

Billions of fans tuned into Sunday's game - which saw Spain triumph over Messi's Argentina 1-0 - after a fraught second half, which saw the teams play into 30 mins of extra time.

Ferran Torres netted the winning goal in the 106th minute - with a devastated Messi watching on.

As well as a halftime show, the World Cup final also included a closing ceremony that featured performances and appearances from Post Malone, Cruise, Nicole Scherzinger, influencer IShowSpeed, Oscar winner Jennifer Hudson, Robbie Williams and Italian singer Laura Pausini.

Stars including Tom Cruise, Timothee Chalamet, Kylie Jenner, Matt Damon and Adrien Brody joined the crowds for the final.

Spanish actor Javier Bardem, skiing legend Lindsey Vonn and actress Julia Garner were also in attendance for the FIFA Gold Carpet event ahead of the final.

Tom Cruise flashed a giddy grin as he sauntered through the stadium ahead of his special appearance at the closing ceremony

Matt Damon and Argentinian wife Luciana Barroso looked giddy as they arrived

Thousands of fans and media members faced massive lines to enter the stadium for the World Cup final on Sunday amid several reports of security struggling to manage the situation

Will Ferrell was in attendance for the huge match

Julia Garner was in attendance to support close pal Madonna ahead of her halftime show

Lindsey Vonn looked stylish as she posed up ahead of the game

Brazil legend Ronaldo Nazario attended with wife Celina Locks

England icon John Terry and Argentina legend Diego Simeone were in attendance

World Cup final day got off to a chaotic start at MetLife Stadium with fans forced to wait for hours outside of the venue amid reports of technological glitches scanning tickets and security staff unsure of how to manage the crowds.

The attendance of President Donald Trump meant that airport-style security measures were also being enforced for everyone making their way inside of the venue.

The game was set to be the most expensive to attend in the history of sport - on Sunday morning, the cheapest ticket available on most resale websites was starting at around $7,000.

FIFA encouraged fans to arrive early in order to participate in the World Cup closing ceremony, scheduled to begin around 90 minutes before the game itself kicks off.

But it is standard procedure for fans to arrive early for additional security checks whenever Trump attends a sporting event - and he has made it to plenty in his second term as President, ranging from the Ryder Cup to the Super Bowl.

Post Malone performed ahead of the final

Cruise kept his look casual in a black tee and jeans as he posed for selfies with queuing fans, while flanked by bodyguards

The star looked excited ahead of the final

Robbie Williams, Nicole Scherzinger and Laura Pausini performed Desire

Man of the hour and Argentina captain Lionel Messi winked at fans as he arrived for the final - before his team heartbreakingly lost to Spain 1-0

A devastated Messi was seen looking dejected after losing

Even on the live television coverage, the stadium was bare with a little over an hour until that closing ceremony began.

Soccer greats such as Brazil World Cup winner Ronaldo, former England captain John Terry and former Argentina player Diego Simeone all appeared carefree as they entered the stadium in good time before the game.

Argentina were narrow underdogs against Spain, the European champions, despite being the holders after winning the 2022 tournament in Qatar.

Trump is expected to hand the World Cup trophy over to the winning team after the game.

Sports.title: World Cup final referee suffers embarrassing spray malfunction... leaving Spain star covered in foam
Sports.content:
World Cup final referee Slavko Vincic suffered an embarrassing moment with the eyes of the world on him during Sunday's World Cup final in New Jersey.

Vincic was appointed to officiate the sport's biggest game - an honor the Slovenian described as a 'dream.'

But after awarding Spain a free-kick in the second half of their clash with Argentina, Vincic suffered a malfunction with his vanishing spray.

As he tried to pull the canister from his back pocket, Vincic inadvertently squirted off its contents right into the face of an unwitting Spain winger Alex Baena, who standing directly behind the ref.

Fortunately for Baena, the mixture of water and propellant gases stream did not force him out of the game. He remained on until the 75th minute, when he was replaced by Nico Williams.

Fans naturally tried to blame the mishap on some nefarious plot to benefit Team Argentina, which ultimately lost the game, 1-0.

The referee has a spray foam malfunction 😅 pic.twitter.com/NV3l6mUHVv — FOX Sports (@FOXSports) July 19, 2026

As he tried to pull the canister from his back pocket, Slavko Vincic inadvertently let off some of the disappearing spray - right into the face of an unwitting Spanish winger Alex Baena

Alex Baena of Spain gestures during the World Cup. He was taken out of the game in the 75th

Alex Baena #15 of Spain argues a call with referee Slavko Vincic during Sunday's final

'Ref trying to blind Alex so Argentinians have a chance,' read a post on X.

Interestingly, it was Argentina fans who were nervous about Vincic ahead of Sunday’s final.

Vincic is a highly experienced referee, having officiated the 2024 Champions League final between Real Madrid and Borussia Dortmund at Wembley, as well as Spain's Euro 2024 semi-final victory over France on their way to becoming champions.

However, it is not only his colorful past, including being 'wrongly' arrested at a 'sex party' in 2020, that has raised concerns in the Argentine media. Much of the apprehension centered on his history with the national team.

The 46-year-old made his World Cup debut at Qatar 2022 and officiated Argentina's shock opening defeat to Saudi Arabia. Notably, that remains the last match involving Argentina that he has overseen, while Lionel Messi & Co. have not lost a World Cup match since, recovering from that early setback to lift the trophy by defeating France on penalties in the final.

Vincic has officiated three matches at this World Cup: the 1-1 group-stage draw between Brazil and Morocco, Algeria's 2-1 win over Jordan, and Mexico's victory over Ecuador in the Round of 32.

On Sunday, Vincic’s biggest impact came in stoppage time when he issued a red card to Argentina’s Enzo Fernández, leaving coach Lionel Scaloni without a key midfielder for extra time.

Sports.title: Alan Shearer lets rip at 'stupid' Enzo Fernandez sent off in Spain vs Argentina World Cup final
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer lets rip at 'stupid' Enzo Fernandez sent off in Spain vs Argentina World Cup final

Alan Shearer did not hold back with his verdict of Enzo Fernandez's red card in the World Cup final

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez was shown a red card for a reckless challenge in the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina (Image: BBC Sport)

Alan Shearer ripped into Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernadez after he was sent off in the World Cup final clash with Spain. The Chelsea star had been shown a yellow card midway through the first half for dissent toward the match officials, before being shown a second yellow for a reckless foul on Pau Cubarsi just minutes before the final whistle.

‌



The game was edging toward extra-time when the 25-year-old went flying into a tackle on the halfway line, with Spain posing no real danger to his side. Cubarsi beat Fernandez to the ball, but the Argentinian midfielder made sure he left his mark on his opponent, upending the Spanish defender.

‌



Referee Slavko Vincic wasted no time in showing Fernandez a second yellow, but the Argentinian midfielder still remonstrated with the officials.

‌



Wayne Rooney leaves BBC pundits speechless with brutal review of World Cup half-time show READ MORE :

Lisandro Martinez in floods of tears as Man Utd star suffers World Cup final agony READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Lionel Messi and Fernandez were both seen arguing with the officials, appearing to call for Marc Cucurella to be shown a red card for covering his mouth with his hand after the original red card incident.

Nothing was given and the Argentinian midfielder was handed his marching orders.

‌



Speaking on co-commentary, Shearer said: "He might just have cost his team massively, because you know now that Argentina are going to try to take it to penalties. With him already being on a yellow card for something stupid - backchatting to the referee.

"And when you're on a yellow, you cannot, cannot make a challenge like that. That is stupid from him, it really is.

"I mean how daft is that from Enzo Fernandez? He's on a yellow card for dissent. Not for the tackel, for dissent. And he knows that, because that didn't happen long ago.

‌



"So for him to go into a challenge like that is crazy. He can protest as much as he wants, but it's the right decision. Gave the referee only one choice, and that was to issue another yellow - therefore the red."

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez was slammed by Alan Shearer after being shown a red card in the World Cup final clash against Spain. (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Wayne Rooney also gave a brutal verdict on the red card ahead of extra-time and said: "It's just a silly tackle. I think he's obviously a little bit late to it as we see here, and on a yellow card you can't just dangle your leg out and give the opposition an opportunity to get you a red card.

‌



"It's silly from Fernandez and it makes it a very different game now for Argentina to get through extra-time. Spain were on top as it was, but this makes it even more difficult."

Argentina did not register a single shot on goal inside the 90 minutes, even with 11 men on the pitch and managed just one touch inside the Spanish box.

Spain were the dominant side with 15 shots, ten of which were on target and 23 touches inside the opposition box, but weren't able to find a way past Emi Martinez as the game went into extra-time.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney leaves BBC pundits speechless with brutal review of World Cup half-time show
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney leaves BBC pundits speechless with brutal review of World Cup half-time show

Wayne Rooney made his feelings about the World Cup half-time show crystal clear

View Image Wayne Rooney was left furious (Image: BBC Sport)

Manchester United and England legend Wayne Rooney branded the World Cup final half-time show 'crap' in a brutally honest verdict. The opening 45 minutes of Argentina and Spain ended 0-0 with the European champions the better of the two sides at the break before a star-studded cast took to the pitch.

‌



The World Cup final has already come under major scrutiny with the pre-match show delaying kick-off by six minutes. While Donald Trump's appearance at the Met Life Stadium caused major delays for fans and members of the media getting into the ground due to heightened security measures.

‌



Spain were the more attacking of the two sides, with Argentina failing to register a single shot in the opening 45 minutes, while the European champions went close through Lamine Yamal and Mikel Oyarzabal.

‌

When the half-time whistle blew, players quickly left the field of play and it was a huge 27 minutes and 18 seconds until they returned, with the half-time show taking place.

As per the International Football Association Board rules, the half-time break should be no longer than 15 minutes, with the interval in breach of those rules.

‌



Justin Bieber, Madonna, Shakira, Gustavo Dudamel and BTS all performed in the half-time show, which was curated by Chris Martin from Coldplay. However, Rooney wasn't impressed.

With the conversation following an advert promoting the BBC, host Gabby Logan added: “I’ll tell you what else you get on the BBC: honest reviews”.

‌



FIFA president Gianni Infantino announced plans for the show – which was curated by Coldplay frontman Chris Martin – in March last year.

Fans were left shocked to see Madonna arrive into the stadium on a buggy with Brazilian legends Ronaldo and Ronaldinho driving the cart.

Sports.title: World Cup fans issue the same complaint about half-time show as Spain vs Argentina delayed
Sports.content:
World Cup fans issue the same complaint about half-time show as Spain vs Argentina delayed

The World Cup final between Spain and Argentina played host to an extended half-time break at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey as Coldplay, Justin Biber and Shakira took centre stage from Lionel Messi and co

View 3 Images The FIFA World Cup 2026 final half-time break lasted 27 minutes (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

World Cup final fans have fumed over the length of the half-time show at MetLife Stadium as Spain and Argentina were forced to take an extended break. The finalists were forced to wait a massive 27minutes and 18 seconds to return to the field.

‌



In an unprecedented move, FIFA's showpiece event saw a planned break that extended beyond the traditional 15 minutes. The show itself, comprising the likes of Madonna, Justin Bieber, Shakira and K-pop band BTS, was expected to be 11 minutes long with additional time required to set up and take down the performance infrastructure.

‌



World football's governing body declined to clarify how long the interval at this year's World Cup final would be on multiple occasions. But, after backlash over the possibility of a 30-minute break, the intention was for the break to last a total of 17 minutes.

‌



Safe to say, the break was too long for most fans, even in a match that was harder to watch than most.

"This is actually disgraceful I cant lie," said one fan on social media. Another said: "Horrendously long half time show that nobody cares to watch btw @FIFA do better"

‌



"I much preferred football when it was a game of two halfs and half-time was barely long enough for the manager to swear at the players and throw teacups round the dressing room," added another.

"I hope with this really long half time, there won’t be another hydration break…" pleaded a further fan. "This half time show is over the top and too long. When is the second half starting?!" said another.

Coldplay's Chris Martin curated the performance, which also featured Nigerian singer Burna Boy, Philharmonic director Gustavo Dudamel, and PS22 Chorus featuring Coldplay. The likes of Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal were forced into an extended break in New Jersey.

‌



View 3 Images Ronaldinho, Madonna and Ronaldo started the half-time show (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

The BBC and ITV were initially not going to broadcast the show and planned to focus on the highlights and analysis from the opening 45 minutes. However, with the break extended, it was deemed possible to broadcast analysis and the on-pitch exploits at the break.

Gary Neville found something to like about the show. Speaking on ITV, he said: "I quite enjoyed it, let's hope the second half picks up and there's loads of energy in that."

‌



On BBC, Wayne Rooney's verdict was less kind. "I'll be honest, mine (highlight) was when it finished," he said.

View 3 Images Justin Bieber performs (Image: Getty Images)

"I like lot of those artists but I thought it was crap. I did, honestly. It just didn't get me going. I want the football to come back on. I like Burna Boy, I like Bieber, I like Shakira. That was flat."

Last summer, FIFA also saw an extended break for the Club World Cup final. They flaunted the rules regarding the length of time between halves for the clash between Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain where the interval stretched to 25 minutes.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez in floods of tears as Man Utd star suffers World Cup final agony
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez in floods of tears as Man Utd star suffers World Cup final agony

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez suffered a cruel injury blow during the first half of the World Cup final

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez was in tears after being forced off with an injury in the World Cup final against Spain (Image: (Photo by Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images))

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez was spotted in floods of tears after being forced off the pitch during the World Cup final against Spain. The 28-year-old started the final in the heart of defence alongside Tottenham Hotspur defender Cristian Romero, but had to be replaced just before the half-time interval with an injury.

‌



It was a tight, nervy first half display from both teams, though Spain looked the most likely to score with Argentina failing to register a single shot inside the opening 45 minutes. Marc Cucurella had just curled an effort just wide of Emi Martinez's goal in the 43rd minute, when Martinez hit the floor.

‌



The United defender had been booked for a late foul on Mikel Oyarzabal just moments earlier, for stopping a Spanish counter attack in its tracks. However, 'The Butcher' was unable to continue and was replaced by former Manchester City defender Nicolas Otamendi in the 44th minute.

‌



Donald Trump brutally booed at World Cup final as Spain and Argentina fans unite READ MORE :

Gary Lineker makes instant England prediction after France and responds to Bukayo Saka READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Martinez left the pitch in tears after being unable to carry on. The former United defender was consoled by Martinez before making his way off the pitch.

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez is consoled by Emi Martinez before he is replaced in the World Cup final vs Spain (Image: (Photo by Hector Vivas - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

‌



The United defender has been a mainstay in the Argentina defence en route to the final, but was visibly distraught after making his way off. He was seen crying, with his head in his hands on the bench.

Argentina were second best throughout the first half, with Spain boasting 65 per cent possession, registering three shots, two of which came on target.

The European champions got off to a fast start when Lamine Yamal burst into the box just five minutes into the game. The Barcelona winger tried to cross into the box, but the ball fell to Dani Olmo on the edge of the area.

‌



The Barca playmaker found Yamal in acres of space inside the 18-yard box, driving to the byline and trying to pick out the bottom corner.

However, a combination of both Lisandro Martinez and Emi Martinez kept the young Spanish star at bay.

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez's World Cup final participation was cut short (Image: BBC Sport)

Article continues below

Argentina were content to sit behind the ball with Lionel Messi as their sole man in attack. Spain kept probing and Oyarzabal called Martinez into action again in the 39th minute.

Fabian Ruiz poked the ball through to the Spanish striker, who rifled a first time left-footed effort down low into the corner, but Martinez was equal to it, keeping the score locked at 0-0 at the half-time interval.

Sports.title: Donald Trump brutally booed at World Cup final as Spain and Argentina fans unite
Sports.content:
Donald Trump brutally booed at World Cup final as Spain and Argentina fans unite

Donald Trump was booed by fans at the 2026 World Cup final at MetLife Stadium just seconds after the national anthem

View 2 Images U.S. President Donald Trump was booed by fans inside the Met Life Stadium at the World Cup final (Image: (Photo by Eva Marie Uzcategui - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

Argentina and Spain fans made their feelings about Donald Trump crystal clear in booing the United States president when he appeared on the big screen at the World Cup Final. Trump had not attended the World Cup until the final, which caused a major headache for those attending the game.

‌



Federal agents, local law enforcement and private security firms had reportedly been mapping out Sunday's security operation for approximately two years, expecting the president to attend the tournament's showpiece event. However, technical problems meant scores of spectators and members of the media faced long delays getting into MetLife Stadium as measures were put in place following Trump's decision to attend.

‌



This, combined with his involvement with FIFA and Folarin Balogun's red card suspension being overturned, resulted in a mixed reception.

‌



Gary Lineker makes instant England prediction after France and responds to Bukayo Saka READ MORE :

Donald Trump picks his World Cup winner and makes request to Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Shortly before kick-off, just seconds after the national anthem concluded, Trump appeared on the giant screens inside MetLife Stadium.

The cheers that had accompanied the anthem quickly gave way to a chorus of boos, whistles, and jeers directed at the president, who had arrived via the Marine One helicopter and made a dramatic flyover of MetLife Stadium before the match got under way.

‌



Trump had been keen to avoid a repeat of his viral New York Knicks moment, while security teams left absolutely nothing to chance. F-16 fighter jets, military marksmen, and thousands of FBI agents were deployed to safeguard MetLife Stadium and the surrounding airspace.

The match has been designated a "Level 1" special event - the highest security classification in the US - putting it on a par with presidential inaugurations and State of the Union addresses.

View 2 Images United States President Donald Trump was booed (Image: Getty Images)

‌



A strictly enforced no-fly zone will cover the New York and New Jersey area from Friday through to Sunday's World Cup final, with snipers stationed on stadium rooftops and a heavily fortified perimeter set to cause considerable delays for supporters.

Once the final whistle blows and either Spain or Argentina are crowned champions, Trump is expected to hand over the iconic World Cup trophy to the victorious captain alongside FIFA president Gianni Infantino.

The 80-year-old was part of the celebrations when Chelsea lifted the trophy after beating Paris Saint-Germain in the Club World Cup Final last summer.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Trump and Infantino have cultivated a remarkably close bond - unlike anything previously witnessed between a FIFA president and a world leader - which culminated in the extraordinary inaugural awarding of the FIFA Peace Prize last December at the World Cup draw.

Ahead of the World Cup Final, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt defended the sheer scale of the security operation, framing Trump's attendance as the crowning moment of the entire tournament.

Article continues below

"His attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure and most successful World Cup in American history," Leavitt said.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker’s son won thousands with stunning seven-fold World Cup final bet
Sports.content:
Gary Lineker’s son won thousands with stunning seven-fold World Cup final bet

George Lineker will be hoping to repeat the trick when Argentina and Spain clash in Sunday's World Cup final

View Image Gary Lineker's son George landed a monster bet at the World Cup 2022 in Qatar (Image: WireImage)

Gary Lineker was one of England’s greatest World Cup heroes during his playing days. The former Three Lions striker won the Golden Boot at Mexico in 1986 and finished his international career with 10 World Cup goals – a national record that stood for 40 years before Harry Kane finally overtook him earlier this summer.

‌



He is also a familiar face at the tournament as a broadcaster, firstly fronting the BBC’s live coverage for decades and now starring on Netflix with his hugely popular The Rest Is Football podcast. And one of his sons also has a memorable World Cup story to tell as well.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The 2022 final in Qatar is widely regarded as one of the greatest matches in football history, with Lionel Messi inspiring Argentina to victory over France after an extraordinary 3-3 draw that featured a Kylian Mbappe hat-trick before a dramatic penalty shootout. It also proved unforgettable for Gary’s eldest son, George, who landed a sizeable four-figure payout after placing an ambitious seven-fold accumulator on the match.

The 34-year-old entrepreneur staked just £20.03 at odds of 170/1, walking away with a tidy return of £4,276.40. George correctly predicted that both Messi and Mbappe would find the net, while also backing the score to be 2-2 after 90 minutes.

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

‌



He also successfully tipped Argentina to lift the trophy on penalties, with his remaining selections centred on the total number of corners and yellow cards shown during the match. Sharing the winning bet slip on social media, he joked: “If anyone deserves to win a bet, I think it’s me. Thank you all.”

Gary Lineker appears on BBC high earners list despite quitting over a year ago READ MORE :

“Haha…you were due one. Congrats mate,” replied Piers Morgan, while his son Spencer quipped: “The only good thing to come out of this.”

That triumph in Qatar finally completed Messi’s glittering career, with the Argentina captain finally lifting the one major trophy that had previously eluded him. Widely regarded as the greatest footballer of all time, the 39-year-old now has the chance to make even more history by becoming a back-to-back World Cup winner.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Argentina booked their place in Sunday’s final after a dramatic comeback victory over England on Wednesday evening, with Messi pulling the strings once again by providing two crucial assists. George Lineker will no doubt be hoping lightning strikes twice as he looks to land another money-spinning World Cup final punt.

Sports.title: Scottie Scheffler breaks silence on Bryson DeChambeau penalty controversy at The Open
Sports.content:
Scottie Scheffler breaks silence on Bryson DeChambeau penalty controversy at The Open

Bryson DeChambeau was handed a two-shot penalty during The Open after he was deemed to have improved his lie during his second round, with world number one Scottie Scheffler now weighing in on the matter

View 2 Images Scottie Scheffler has broken his silence on the Bryson DeChambeau controversy (Image: Sky Sports)

Controversial golf star Bryson DeChambeau is 'definitely not a cheater', according to world number one Scottie Scheffler, after the bolshy American received a two-shot penalty at The Open following an inadvertent breach when he improved his lie during his second round.

‌



Scheffler believes more players are pushing the lines on what is permitted on the course and he has suggested that the type of incidents which landed DeChambeau in hot water require stricter oversight, with the penalised superstar facing greater scrutiny than most. However, he believes that DeChambeau was sloppy rather than deliberately dishonest in his actions.

‌



The four-time major champion had previously stayed tight-lipped on the subject, stating: "I do have a ton to say. I haven't decided exactly what I want to say publicly yet."

‌



But now he's broken his silence on the controversy. "I think that opens up a greater discussion that - all I can really say is I think maybe we need to be a little bit more strict in the way that we are policing guys," Scheffler remarked.

"But it's a little bit of a balance because you've got certain guys like a Bryson who every shot he hits is going to be shown on TV. When you have camera angles that are far away, things can look different than they do when you're right there.

Scottie Scheffler rages at The Open as tempers flare in dramatic scenes READ MORE :

"We've done a good job of - I don't know, I hate saying stuff out here because I don't want anything to get taken out of context. All I'll say is Bryson, I've known him for a long time, and he's a lot of things, but he's definitely not a cheater.

‌



"I've never seen him cheat once, whether we were having a putting contest on the putting green or chipping contest, or anytime we played amateur golf, I never saw anything suspicious.

"When you're watching him there from that camera angle, maybe he was a touch careless around his ball, but I don't think he did anything intentionally.

View 2 Images Bryson DeChambeau was angered by his penalty following the second round of The Open (Image: Getty)

‌



"We've seen penalties happen with - like you remember Jon Rahm a couple years ago at the Memorial when his ball moved in the rough, and it's like to the naked eye, can you really tell that?".

"I think sometimes it's just a difficult position in the game of golf. When I was growing up, if this was the line between things that were - like if this was the line, here are the rules and this was the right side of it and this is when you're doing things against the rule, you always tried to stray really far that way. I feel like at times, sometimes you see players maybe push it a little bit further than they should."

Two-time US Open champion DeChambeau became embroiled in a prolonged and heated exchange with R&A rules officials before the penalty was handed down. That post-round confrontation resulted in a delay to the release of Saturday's tee times.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Rory McIlroy made clear he felt it was beside the point whether DeChambeau had cheated or not, expressing his frustration at the American's conduct. The Ryder Cup stalwart accused DeChambeau of holding the tournament to ransom and was scathing in his assessment.

"I think there's no doubt that he improved the line of his backswing," McIlroy said. "Whether it was careless or whether it was intentional, I don't think it matters. Hopefully it was careless, but I think the two-shot penalty was justified for sure.

Article continues below

"I won't pretend to defend Bryson," he continued. "I'm not particularly fond of him. I think a lot of it's performative. I think a lot of it's for attention.

"To hold the tournament hostage like that, and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn't feel like it was a great look."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
